issue_body:
## What
A PagerDuty connector, so that someone who connects their PagerDuty account in Switch Console can let their agents read incidents, services and on-call schedules, and acknowledge or resolve incidents, as them.

## Why
Agents helping with incidents need to know what's firing and who's on call.

## How
PagerDuty has an official remote MCP server at `https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp` (EU variant) that accepts an API key (`Token token=…`) or OAuth, but **no dynamic registration** ([docs](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/pagerduty-mcp-server)). The `api_key` shape is probably simplest; a static OAuth app is the other option.

Add a new entry, `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/pagerduty/`.

Follow **[Adding a connector](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/blob/main/docs/design/service-connections-v2.md#adding-a-connector)** in the service connections v2 design doc. A connector is usually a catalog entry plus a skill, with no code, in one of three shapes:
1. a remote MCP server with OAuth (example: `catalog/atlassian/`)
2. a command-line tool with OAuth (example: `catalog/google-workspace/`)
3. a key the person pastes in (`adapter: api_key`, with `mcp` or `cli`; example: `catalog/datadog/`)

Prefer OAuth with dynamic registration where the vendor offers it, then a static OAuth app, then a key, and say in the PR why you chose that shape. If the vendor fits none of them, comment on this issue before writing broker code.

Locally, turn connections on with `FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED=service_connections`.

**Rules every connector follows:**
- The token or key never reaches the coding tool (env, args or files); the session host makes the calls
- Ask for the least access that works: no admin, org-wide or delete scopes without a written reason. Offer a read-only level if the vendor supports one
- OAuth stays strict: HTTPS, PKCE S256, no new redirect hosts; don't loosen the loader's checks
- CLIs run without a shell, from the vendor's official release pinned by SHA-256, with auth/config/admin commands denied
- No real data in the repo: no tokens, tenant URLs or account ids in fixtures or screenshots
- The logo is the official mark (viewBox and paths only), credited in `NOTICE.md`

## Done when
- [ ] `connections/catalog/pagerduty/connection.yaml` is complete and `enabled: true`, with comments on anything the vendor needs turned on and anything measured rather than documented (e.g. token lifetime)
- [ ] `skill/SKILL.md` describes the tasks, tools and limits, with safe defaults (read before writing, confirm before deleting or closing), and never mentions credentials
- [ ] It shows up in Switch Console's Connections with its name and logo, and connecting works (read-only and read-write, if both are offered)
- [ ] Granted to an agent, its tools work in a session from a room; turning the grant off stops the session's access within a minute
- [ ] An expiring token is renewed without the user doing anything (OAuth)
- [ ] Disconnecting removes access (and revokes at the vendor where possible; for keys, the UI says Switch can't revoke them)
- [ ] The token or key appears nowhere in the transcript, the room or the logs
- [ ] Loader tests for the entry (`core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py`)
- [ ] A short video of connect → grant → agent uses it in a room → grant off

## Out of scope
Webhooks from the vendor into rooms; tool classification by level; connecting from the web dashboard.

prs.title: feat(connections): add the PagerDuty connector (closes #825)
prs.author: talibot-agent
prs.body:
Closes #825

## What
A PagerDuty connector: a person pastes a PagerDuty **User API key** and picks their service region; agents granted the connection get PagerDuty's hosted MCP tools (incidents, alerts, services, on-call schedules, escalation policies, status pages) as that person.

## Why this shape (`api_key`)
- PagerDuty's hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp`, EU `https://mcp.eu.pagerduty.com/mcp`) supports OAuth only with a static client and **no dynamic client registration** ([docs](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/pagerduty-mcp-server)). A key needs no operator setup, so the connector works on every server out of the box. A static-OAuth variant can be added later beside it.
- A **User** key (not General Access) is asked for: some tools (e.g. `list_incidents` scoped to `assigned`/`teams`) need user-level auth, and the identity call `GET https://api.{region}/users/me` names the person (`user.id`, labelled `user.email`). A General Access key has no user and fails that check, which is intended.
- Region is a choice, never free text, so it can only route to `pagerduty.com` or `eu.pagerduty.com`.

## Rules
- The key never reaches the coding tool: `token: { kind: pass_through, max_lifetime: null }`, headers are filled by the session host.
- Least access: PagerDuty has no read-only user key, so `tools: pass_through` (as the loader requires for `api_key`) and the description and skill say plainly that it can write. The skill defaults to read first and confirm before acknowledging/resolving, creating incidents (which pages people), deleting, or posting to a public status page; it treats alert payloads as untrusted.
- Logo: Simple Icons 16.33.0 `pagerduty` (CC0), viewBox and path only, credited in `NOTICE.md`; brand colour `#06AC38`.

## Tests
- New `test_the_shipped_pagerduty_entry_signs_in_as_a_user_and_picks_its_region`; catalog, registry and gateway catalog tests updated for the new enabled entry.
- `pytest tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py tests/switch_core/gateway/test_connection_catalog.py`: 152 passed locally; the 9 that need Postgres via Docker could not run in my sandbox and are left to CI. `ruff check` clean.
- Live check: `api.pagerduty.com/users/me`, `api.eu.pagerduty.com/users/me`, `mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp` and `mcp.eu.pagerduty.com/mcp` all answer 401 to a bad key, so the URLs are right.

## Still to do (draft)
- [ ] Video of connect → grant → agent uses it in a room → grant off (needs a PagerDuty trial account)

_This PR was written by Tali, an AI agent, for the Flip the Switch hackathon._

## What
Adds the official declarative PagerDuty connector to Switch Core's service connections catalog.

## Why
Enables operators and users to connect their PagerDuty account in Switch Console so agents can inspect incidents, check on-call schedules, explore escalation policies, and coordinate incident response in rooms.

## Details
- Follows the declarative `adapter: api_key` pattern documented in `docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`.
- **Endpoints:**
  - US: `https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp` and REST `https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me`
  - EU: `https://mcp.eu.pagerduty.com/mcp` and REST `https://api.eu.pagerduty.com/users/me`
- **Authentication:** Validates API key against `/users/me` with `Authorization: Token token={api_key}`, extracting `user.id` and `user.email`.
- **MCP Server:** Passes through to `https://mcp.{region}/mcp` with `Authorization: Token token={api_key}` header.
- **Skill:** Provides safe operational guidance for incident management and summarizing alert data without exposing credentials.
- **Console UI:** Includes official Simple Icons `pagerduty.svg` vector icon and attribution in `NOTICE.md`.
- **Tests:** Full unit test coverage in `test_loader.py` validating schema compliance.

Closes #825

Adds PagerDuty to the connection catalog, so someone can connect their PagerDuty account in Switch Console and let their agents read incidents, services and on-call, and acknowledge or resolve incidents, as them.

Closes #825

- `catalog/pagerduty/connection.yaml`: an `api_key` entry for PagerDuty's hosted MCP server. The user picks the US or EU service region (a fixed choice, never a free-text host) and pastes a user key; both the MCP server and the identity call get `Authorization: Token token=<key>`.
- Identity is `GET https://api.{region}/users/me`. It only answers for a user's key, so an account-wide key is refused at connect and every connection acts as one person, with that person's role.
- `skill/SKILL.md`: read the incident before changing it, acknowledge/resolve only what the user named, ask before adding responders, creating incidents or posting to a status page, and leave services, schedules and escalation settings alone unless asked.
- Logo from Simple Icons (CC0), credited in the logos' `NOTICE.md`; brand colour `#06AC38`; display name in `service-notices.ts`.
- A short PagerDuty section in `docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`.

**Why a key and not OAuth:** PagerDuty's MCP server has no dynamic client registration. A static OAuth app would work, but it means a client to register and configure per deployment; a user key fits the existing `api_key` shape with no new code, and PagerDuty enforces the person's own permissions. There's no read-only mode on the server side, so the skill is careful about writes, and the PR doesn't claim one.

- New loader test pins the fields, the region choices, the identity call and the MCP headers; registry tests check it gets an `ApiKeyAdapter` with nothing to set up on the server.
- New adapter test runs `identify()` against a mock transport and checks it calls `https://api.eu.pagerduty.com/users/me` with the right header and maps `user.id` / `user.email`.
- `pytest core/tests/switch_core/connections`: 224 passed. The 131 errors are the Postgres-backed tests, which need Docker for testcontainers and couldn't start in my environment; they error the same way on `main`.
- `just check` (ruff format + lint) and `just typecheck` (mypy) are clean.

prs.title: feat(connections): add PagerDuty connector (#825)
prs.author: jmass-ggg
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements the PagerDuty connector catalog entry, API-token validation, regional MCP configuration, Console branding, agent investigation skill, and automated tests.

The connector follows the existing Switch API-key architecture and preserves the security policy for non-expiring credentials.

**Important:** The current broker rejects non-expiring API-key connections through `key_never_expires`. This PR implements the catalog and supporting functionality but does not yet provide a working live connection or agent grant.

Related to #825.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Switch Console"] --> B["PagerDuty User API Token + Region"]
    B --> C{"Switch Broker Policy"}
    C -->|"Current: key_never_expires"| D["Connection Blocked"]

    E["Configured Integration Path"] -.-> F["PagerDuty /users/me Identity"]
    F -.-> G["Regional MCP Endpoint"]
    G -.-> H["Session Host MCP Proxy"]
    H -.-> I["PagerDuty Remote MCP Server"]
    I -.-> J["Incidents, Services, On-call Schedules"]

    D --> K["Execution Path Requires Follow-up"]
```

*Dashed arrows describe the intended integration, not a completed end-to-end connection.*

## Implementation

* Added the PagerDuty connector catalog entry.
* Implemented User API-token authentication configuration using the documented `Authorization: Token token=...` format.
* Added fixed supported global/US and EU region choices.
* Configured identity validation through the documented `/users/me` endpoint.
* Added a credential-free PagerDuty investigation skill.
* Added support documentation for token revocation and permission boundaries.
* Added the PagerDuty SVG and Console icon integration.
* Updated the connector asset attribution.
* Added loader, registry, gateway, and adapter tests.
* Added tests for regional selection, authentication templates, invalid identity responses, and security restrictions.

The agent skill encourages inspection of incident context before action and requires explicit authorisation for operational changes such as acknowledging, resolving, or reassigning incidents.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Connector, broker and catalog Python tests | 424 passed |
| PagerDuty HTTP boundary tests | 2 passed |
| Affected workspace tests after corrections | 19 passed |
| Console icon/agent tests | 53 passed |
| Host credential/MCP/redaction tests | 52 passed |
| Ruff and Mypy | Passed |
| Console lint, typecheck and build | Passed |
| Git whitespace checks | Passed |

Earlier catalog assertion failures were corrected before the agent's final commit.

## Security

* Rejects unsupported regions and malformed credentials.
* Keeps the User API token within Switch's existing credential boundaries.
* Sanitises identity and transport errors.
* Refuses unexpected identity-request redirects.
* Preserves the prohibition on issuing non-expiring credentials directly to agents.
* Documents that disconnecting from Switch does not revoke a PagerDuty API token at the vendor.
* Requires explicit instructions for incident-modifying actions.

## Blocking limitation

The existing broker policy returns `key_never_expires` for credentials with an indefinite lifetime.

The PagerDuty User API token is represented using `max_lifetime: null`, so the current implementation cannot complete a live connection or grant the service to an agent.

This PR intentionally preserves the existing security restriction.

A separately reviewed execution strategy is required before the issue's end-to-end acceptance criteria can be fulfilled.

## Remaining acceptance criteria

* Supported live connection and agent execution.
* Authorised PagerDuty test account.
* Incident, service, and on-call tool calls with test data.
* Permission-denial and grant-removal verification.
* Credential-disclosure checks.
* Demonstration video.

## Commit

`ba7a2a59`

This PR provides the catalog integration and automated validation for review. It is not presented as a complete resolution of #825.

prs.title: feat(connections): add PagerDuty connector (#825)
prs.author: ADITYASINGH1206
prs.body:
Closes #825

## What this adds

PagerDuty as an enabled connector. People connect their own PagerDuty account from Switch Console, and their agents can read incidents, services, schedules and who is on call. With write access, agents can also acknowledge, resolve, reassign and annotate incidents, as that person.

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Catalog | `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/pagerduty/connection.yaml` (`enabled: true`) and `skill/SKILL.md` |
| Console | `pagerduty.svg`: Simple Icons mark (CC0), `NOTICE.md` row with the brand guidelines link, brand colour `#06AC38` |
| Setup steps | PagerDuty steps for Connector apps in both the dashboard (`gateway/`) and Switch Console. Without them, it would fall back to the one-line generic step. |
| Docs | A "PagerDuty" section in `docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`, an operator guide `docs/old/pagerduty-setup.md` (listed in `CLAUDE.md`), and a CHANGELOG entry |
| Tests | Loader, adapter conformance, catalog listings, Connector apps (Python, dashboard and Console) |

## Why OAuth (static), not a key

The issue suggests the `api_key` shape as the simplest option. Since `26a2c0f` ("stop handing agents long-lived service credentials"), an entry whose token never expires "cannot be granted, connected or issued". The broker answers `key_never_expires`, and Datadog is in that state today.

A PagerDuty user API key never expires. A key-based entry would therefore be listed but could never reach a room, and "Granted tools work in a room session" couldn't be met.

PagerDuty's hosted MCP server also takes OAuth, with no dynamic registration. That leaves a static OAuth client, which is also ahead of a key in the issue's preference order.

- **Scoped OAuth, not Classic.** Classic gives only blanket `read`/`write`, and its access tokens live 30 days, past the 7-day `max_lifetime` the loader accepts.
- **Scoped OAuth lifecycle.** Access tokens live 1 day and refresh tokens 30 days, with a rolling window of up to a year ([Private Apps, Token Lifetimes](https://docs.pagerduty.com/developer/private-apps)).
- **Real read-only level.** Scoped OAuth gives per-resource scopes, so there is a genuine read-only connection as well as read-write.

## How the entry is built

Facts come from PagerDuty's docs, its OpenAPI specs in `PagerDuty/api-schema` (REST and MCP, as of 2026-10-21), and this repo's adapter code.

- **Endpoints:** `https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/authorize` and `/oauth/token`, named rather than discovered ([OAuth Functionality](https://docs.pagerduty.com/developer/oauth-functionality)). The adapter therefore sends the secret in the form body, as PagerDuty's docs do.
- **PKCE:** Scoped OAuth apps are confidential clients that must use PKCE with S256, which the adapter always sends.
- **Redirect:** `[core]`, Core's own https callback, as Airtable and Google Workspace use. This adds no new redirect hosts, and nothing listens on people's computers.
- **Refresh:** `rotating`. Each refresh returns a new refresh token, and PagerDuty doesn't say whether the old one survives, so refreshes are never raced.
- **Token:** `{ kind: pass_through, max_lifetime: 86400 }`. The MCP spec's `Authorization` parameter accepts `Bearer <token>`.
- **Identity:** `GET https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me`, with `user.id` and `user.email`. The spec says it works only with a user token, never an account-level one. PagerDuty takes the API version from the token unless an Accept header overrides it ([Versioning](https://docs.pagerduty.com/developer/versioning)), so the adapter's `Accept: application/json` is fine.
- **Scopes:** taken from the REST spec's "Scoped OAuth requires" line for the endpoints each of the 18 MCP tools calls.
  - Read: `users.read`, `incidents.read`, `services.read`, `schedules.read`, `oncalls.read`, `escalation_policies.read`, `teams.read`, `change_events.read`.
  - Write adds only `incidents.write`: create, acknowledge, resolve, reassign, notes and responders.
  - Not requested: no admin, delete or org-wide scopes; nothing for status pages, incident workflows or event orchestrations; and no writes to services, schedules or teams. Those tools are listed by the server but refused, and the skill says so.
- **Revocation:** PagerDuty has no endpoint to revoke a single sign-in, so `remove_access` tells people where to revoke their own token (Integrations, OAuth Apps). Until then, the token works until it expires, within a day.
- **`unchecked`:** an unknown scope isn't refused; PagerDuty silently grants a token with only `openid`. Whether the app is installed on other accounts also can't be checked, so the operator is told to connect once to confirm.

## Rules from the issue

- **Token never reaches the coding tool.** It's an OAuth pass-through token, handled like Atlassian's and Airtable's, with no env, args or files.
- **Least access.** Per-resource scopes with a genuine read-only level. Write access is limited to incidents.
- **Strict OAuth.** HTTPS endpoints, PKCE S256, and no new redirect hosts (Core's callback only).
- **No real data.** Tests use the existing fake vendor and placeholder values.
- **Logo.** The official mark from Simple Icons, credited in `NOTICE.md`.

## Tests run locally

Postgres-backed tests were run against a local Postgres 16.

- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy` (641 files), `e2e_surface.py --check`, `gen_artifacts.py --check`: all clean.
- `pytest core/tests/switch_core/connections core/tests/switch_core/gateway`: all pass except `test_tenant_api_routes::...test_removing_a_member_deletes_their_membership`, which fails identically on `main` without this change.
- New tests:
  - `test_the_shipped_pagerduty_entry_signs_in_as_its_docs_say_it_must`
  - `TestPagerDuty` in `adapters/test_oauth.py` (documented endpoints, PKCE S256, space-separated scopes, secret in the body, day-long tokens, refresh, no revocation)
  - Updated catalog and listing tests
- Gateway: `npm run build` passes, and `vitest` passes except two Teams download tests that fail identically on `main` (environment Blob issue).
- Console: `tsgo --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `connection-icon.test.ts` (every catalog slug has a logo and every logo a NOTICE row), and the `connector-apps`, `connectors` and `admin` tests all pass.

## Not verified yet

I have no PagerDuty account in this environment, so nothing here was run against the real vendor. The hand QA from "Adding a connector" and the video need a PagerDuty account with a Scoped OAuth app. Specifically still to confirm:

- How PagerDuty answers Connector apps' made-up-code check: `invalid_grant` is expected. If it answers differently, the configuration path still works.
- That `/users/me` answers with only the scopes above.
- The real token lifetime.

These comments are marked "documented, not measured" in `connection.yaml`.

Out of scope, as listed in the issue: webhooks, tool classification, and connecting from the web dashboard. EU-region accounts (`mcp.eu.pagerduty.com` and `api.eu.pagerduty.com`) aren't covered, because an entry can't pick its endpoints per connection today. That is noted in the entry and the docs.
